newsitem.title: ALBANIA: EC aid held under armed guard in Albania.
newsitem.headline: EC aid held under armed guard in Albania.

text.p: Emergency food supplies from the European Community have arrived in Albania but are in store under armed guard until local authorities deem roads safe enough for distribution, a military spokesman said on Friday.

Lieutenant Colonel Giovanni Bernardi said 940 tonnes of flour from the European Community Humanitarian Office had arrived at the port of Durres, 40 km west of Tirana, and was being unloaded on Friday.
"None of this food will be distributed until the local authorities think the situation is completely under control," Bernardi told a news briefing.

International aid groups estimate one in every 10 of the 3.4 million Albanians is in need of relief since an armed uprising stopped state food supplies to hospitals, orphanages and other institutions.

Food prices have also soared since Albanians took to the streets, raiding state arsenals in the chaos that prevailed after the collapse of five get-rich-quick "pyramid" schemes in which many had invested their life savings.
Over 300 people have been killed and more than 700 injured in the violence and services have ground to a halt.
Armed rebels, who blame President Sali Berisha for the pyramids disaster, remain in control of most of the south of Albania, the poorest nation in Europe.

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) has already distributed 360 tonnes of flour, 36 tonnes of beans and 23 tonnes of vegetable oil to 4,400 destitute families around the small Balkan country where the average monthly wage is $80.
The WFP is planning another shipment of 15,000 tonnes of flour in the next 10 days to supply 400,000 people and bridge the gap until the next wheat harvest in July.
The International Commission of the Red Cross handed out 40 tonnes of food and 15 tonnes of medicines since March 27.
An eight-nation United Nations-approved force of 6,000 soldiers has been assigned to Albania to ensure aid supplies can be delivered safely, securing routes for transport.
The EC Humanitarian Office is hoping to see its supplies distributed within the next 10 days, safety permitting and after the completion of an assessment study.

"By then we should have resolved the whole question of safety of delivery and of ensuring the food gets into the hands of the right people," Robert Cox, deputy director of the humanitarian aid at the EC office told Reuters.

Bernardi said 4,900 soldiers from the Italian-led force have arrived in Albania so far including 2,630 Italians, 930 from France, 300 Spaniards, 630 Greeks, 420 from Turkey, two from Romania, two from Denmark and two from Austria.
The remaining soldiers are expected to arrive by May 4 and will remain in Albania until after a general election that is scheduled for June 29.

So far two soldiers have been injured: a Turkish soldier hit in the hand by a stray bullet while on guard at the international airport and a French soldier injured when a gas stove exploded in his barracks.
Meanwhile rebel leaders and opposition politicians met in the southern port of Vlore on Friday, calling for the troops to be allowed to monitor polling stations during the election.
